    // The weight of one cell shared equally among its four nodes. Equal sharing
    // is not an approximation: each linear shape function integrates to a quarter
    // of the cell volume, so this IS the consistent load vector of a uniform body
    // force.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_force)
    GravityContributions(c: TetrahedronCell, positions: Array<Point3D>, density: Density,
        gravity: Vector3D): Array<DofLoad>
    {
        var share = density.KilogramsPerCubicMeter * c.ToTetrahedron(positions).Volume * 0.25;
        var nodes = c.CellVertices;
        return 12.MapRange(k =>
            DofLoad(DofIndex(nodes[k / 3].Value * 3 + k % 3), gravity.At(k % 3) * share));
    }

    // A uniform traction over one boundary triangle shared equally among its
    // three nodes — again exact rather than lumped, for the same reason: a linear
    // triangle's shape functions each integrate to a third of its area.
    LoadContributions(t: FaceTraction3D, positions: Array<Point3D>): Array<DofLoad>
    {
        var share = t.Face.ToTriangle3D(positions).Area / 3.0;
        var nodes = t.Face.Vertices;
        return 9.MapRange(k =>
            DofLoad(DofIndex(nodes[k / 3].Value * 3 + k % 3), t.Traction.At(k % 3) * share));
    }

    // Every load on the model resolved into degree-of-freedom contributions:
    // nodal forces, then the body force of gravity, then the boundary tractions.
    LoadContributions(model: ElasticModel3D): Array<DofLoad>
        => model.Forces.FlatMap(f => f.LoadContributions)
            .Concatenate(model.Mesh.Cells.FlatMap(c =>
                c.GravityContributions(model.Mesh.Positions, model.Material.Density,
                    model.Gravity)))
            .Concatenate(model.Tractions.FlatMap(t =>
                t.LoadContributions(model.Mesh.Positions)));

    // The load vector in global degree-of-freedom order.
    LoadVector(model: ElasticModel3D): Array<Number>
        => model.LoadContributions.ScatterLoads(model.DofCount);

    // The linear-elastic solve of a solid model: assemble, load, run the
    // constrained conjugate gradient, and read each node's displacement out of
    // the solution vector. The convergence report travels with the answer, so a
    // caller that ignores it still gets the last iterate rather than nothing.
    SolveElastic(model: ElasticModel3D, settings: LinearSolveSettings): ElasticSolution3D
    {
        var solved = model.StiffnessMatrix.SolveConstrained(model.LoadVector,
            model.Constraints, settings);
        var u = solved.Solution;
        return ElasticSolution3D(
            model.Mesh.Positions.Count.MapRange(i =>
                Vector3D(u[i * 3], u[i * 3 + 1], u[i * 3 + 2])),
            solved.Iterations, solved.Residual, solved.Converged);
    }

    //==
    // # Plane analysis
    //
    // The same three steps for an `ElasticModel2D`. Only the component count, the
    // element measure and the choice of Lame pair differ.

    // Two degrees of freedom per mesh position.
    DofCount(model: ElasticModel2D): Integer
        => model.Mesh.Positions.Count * 2;

    // The Lame pair the model's plane idealization implies.
    Moduli(model: ElasticModel2D): LameParameters
        => model.Material.PlaneLameParameters(model.Condition);

    // The assembled global stiffness matrix of a plane model.
    StiffnessMatrix(model: ElasticModel2D): SparseMatrix
    {
        var moduli = model.Moduli;
        var n = model.DofCount;
        return SparseMatrix(n, n, model.Mesh.Faces.FlatMap(f =>
            f.StiffnessEntries(model.Mesh.Positions, model.Thickness, moduli)));
    }

    // A concentrated nodal force resolved onto the two degrees of freedom of its
    // node.
    LoadContributions(f: NodalForce2D): Array<DofLoad>
        => [
            DofLoad(DofIndex(f.Node.Value * 2), f.Force.X),
            DofLoad(DofIndex(f.Node.Value * 2 + 1), f.Force.Y)];

    // The weight of one plane element shared equally among its three nodes,
    // through the modelled thickness.
    GravityContributions(f: TriangleFace, positions: Array<Point2D>, thickness: Length,
        density: Density, gravity: Vector2D): Array<DofLoad>
    {
        var share = density.KilogramsPerCubicMeter * f.ToTriangle2D(positions).Area
            * thickness.Meters / 3.0;
        var nodes = f.Vertices;
        return 6.MapRange(k =>
            DofLoad(DofIndex(nodes[k / 2].Value * 2 + k % 2), gravity.At(k % 2) * share));
    }

    // Every load on a plane model resolved into degree-of-freedom contributions.
    LoadContributions(model: ElasticModel2D): Array<DofLoad>
        => model.Forces.FlatMap(f => f.LoadContributions)
            .Concatenate(model.Mesh.Faces.FlatMap(f =>
                f.GravityContributions(model.Mesh.Positions, model.Thickness,
                    model.Material.Density, model.Gravity)));

    // The load vector in global degree-of-freedom order.
    LoadVector(model: ElasticModel2D): Array<Number>
        => model.LoadContributions.ScatterLoads(model.DofCount);

    // The linear-elastic solve of a plane model.
    SolveElastic(model: ElasticModel2D, settings: LinearSolveSettings): ElasticSolution2D
    {
        var solved = model.StiffnessMatrix.SolveConstrained(model.LoadVector,
            model.Constraints, settings);
        var u = solved.Solution;
        return ElasticSolution2D(
            model.Mesh.Positions.Count.MapRange(i => Vector2D(u[i * 2], u[i * 2 + 1])),
            solved.Iterations, solved.Residual, solved.Converged);
    }

    //==
    // # Recovering strain and stress
    //
    // A displacement field is not what an engineer looks at. Strain is its
    // symmetrised gradient, stress follows from strain by Hooke's law, and von
    // Mises stress is the scalar those two get reduced to before anyone colours a
    // picture with it. Over a constant-gradient element all three are constant,
    // so each is one value per element.

    // The (r, c) entry of the displacement gradient inside a constant-gradient
    // element: the sum over its nodes of displacement component r times shape
    // gradient component c.
    DisplacementGradient(nodal: Array<Vector3D>, gradients: Array<Vector3D>,
        r: Integer, c: Integer): Number
        => nodal.Count.Range.Reduce(0.0, (total, i) =>
            total + nodal[i].At(r) * gradients[i].At(c));

    // The constant strain inside one tetrahedral cell, as the symmetric tensor of
    // TENSOR strains — off-diagonal entries are half the engineering shears,
    // which is what `StrainState3D` documents.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinitesimal_strain_theory)
    ElementStrain(c: TetrahedronCell, positions: Array<Point3D>,
        displacements: Array<Vector3D>): StrainState3D
    {
        var gradients = c.ShapeGradients(positions);
        var nodes = c.CellVertices;
        var nodal = 4.MapRange(i => displacements[nodes[i].Value]);
        return StrainState3D(SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 0),
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 1)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 0)) * 0.5,
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 2)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 0)) * 0.5,
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 1),
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 2)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 1)) * 0.5,
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 2)));
    }
